post.description:
Request a time-limited password-reset link using **either username or email**, not both. This is public account recovery, not administrative password generation.

### Privacy and delivery

Return the same `202` body for known, unknown, ambiguous and ineligible accounts, including account-specific delivery failures. Do not expose account ids, tokens, delivery status or a result lookup URL. Use a common response path and deferred delivery to avoid account-dependent response timing. Log delivery failures privately; this rule applies regardless of the site's username-disclosure setting.

Reuse Moodle's existing recovery eligibility, token expiry, single-use and redemption rules. The email links to Moodle's existing password-reset page. **Requesting a link does not change the password or force a logout.** Ambiguous email matches must not select an arbitrary account.

### Abuse and retries

Apply account-independent request throttling and per-identifier delivery limits. Apply the same identifier-limit behaviour whether or not an account exists; suppress repeated emails without changing the generic acceptance response. Request-level throttling may return `429` with `Retry-After`. Service-wide failure may return a generic `503`; account-specific outcomes remain private. No API authentication or OAuth scope is required.

byEmail.summary: Request a reset link by email
byEmail.description: Request recovery for an email address. The response does not reveal whether a matching, eligible account exists.

byUsername.summary: Request a reset link by username
byUsername.description: Use a username instead of an email address, for example when multiple accounts share an email address.

202.description: Request accepted for consideration. This does not confirm account existence, eligibility or email delivery. No `Location` or delivery receipt is returned.

message.const: If an eligible account matches, password-reset instructions will be sent.

accepted.description: Identical for matching, missing, ambiguous and ineligible accounts.

value.message: If an eligible account matches, password-reset instructions will be sent.

503.description: Recovery is temporarily unavailable for all callers. Never use this response to reveal an account-specific delivery failure.

patch.description:
Set an explicit password through the supported authentication plugin. The password must meet site policy and is **never returned**. This is an administrative operation, not a self-service change-password form.

### Permissions

Token scope: `core_user:user:update`. All callers need system-level `moodle/user:update`. `update:self` alone is insufficient. Reject guest/deleted accounts and authentication mechanisms without supported password management; only site administrators may change another administrator's credentials.

### Behaviour

Set `requirePasswordChange` only when you also want to change that persistent account requirement; omission preserves it. Use Moodle's password lifecycle and session-invalidation policy. No credential email is sent. Repeating the same desired state does not intentionally generate another password, but history/policy checks may reject a repeat. Do not retry blindly after an uncertain result.

Use POST `/user/users/{userId}/password-reset` to generate a temporary password instead. This write-only resource has no readable password representation or ETag; conditional writes are not offered.

setExplicitPassword.summary: Set a password and require a change at next login
setExplicitPassword.description: Administrative credential update using a password that must satisfy site policy. This illustrative password must not be reused.

204.description: Password updated. No response body or password is returned.

post.description:
Submit to the user's singleton password-reset resource to generate a temporary password. **The existing password changes immediately**, and a password change is required at next login. No password or recovery token is returned.

### Permissions

Token scope: `core_user:user:update`. All callers need system-level `moodle/user:update`; `update:self` alone is insufficient. Reject guest/deleted accounts and unsupported password management. Only site administrators may reset another administrator's credentials.

### Delivery and result

Email the password after successful credential replacement unless `sendPasswordEmail` is false. A delivery failure is logged and reported as `failed`; it does not undo the reset. When email is suppressed, arrange access separately. Use Moodle's password lifecycle and session-invalidation policy.

Return `200` with the immediate, non-secret outcome. No individually addressable reset record, result GET, retention period or `Location` header is introduced.

### Retries

Each accepted POST replaces the password again. **Do not repeat POST to retry email delivery or resolve an uncertain result.** This contract offers no duplicate-request protection. Public reset-link requests use POST `/user/password-reset` instead.

emailTemporaryPassword.summary: Generate and email a temporary password
emailTemporaryPassword.description: Replace the existing password, send the new password by email and require a password change at next login.

suppressEmail.summary: Generate a temporary password without email
suppressEmail.description: Replace the existing password without emailing or returning it. Arrange access separately before using this option.

200.description: Password replaced. The immediate outcome reports email failure separately; it does not undo the reset. No reset record or result URL is created.

emailAccepted.description: The password was replaced. Mail-transport acceptance does not guarantee inbox delivery.

emailFailed.description: The password was still replaced and the mail failure was logged. Do not repeat the reset POST to resend the email.

post.description:
Provision one Moodle account, including optional profile and custom fields. This is **not self-registration** and does not create an external identity-provider account.

### Permissions

Token scope: `core_user:user:create`. All callers need system-level `moodle/user:create`; populating initial fields requires no additional read/update permission.

### Passwords

- For password-based authentication, supply `password` **or** `generatePassword: true`, never both.
- Generated passwords require a change at first login. Email is sent after creation unless `sendPasswordEmail: false`.
- With email suppressed, arrange access separately through password reset or credential provisioning.
- Explicit passwords must meet site policy; no automatic email or forced change follows.
- Authentication without Moodle-managed passwords rejects both password supply and generation. **Passwords are never returned.**

### Creation and result

Validate and save account, profile and custom fields atomically, applying defaults and required/unique field rules. Initial provisioning is distinct from later auth-plugin field locks. Follow Moodle's creation lifecycle, emitting `user_created` after the supplied data is saved.

Return `201` with an `{id, username}` receipt and numeric-id resource URL in `Location`. No ETag is returned; an authorised GET retrieves the representation and ETag. See the `201` response for email delivery outcomes.

explicitPassword.summary: Create an account with an explicit password
explicitPassword.description: Create a manual-authentication account using an initial password that must satisfy the site's password policy. No credential email is sent, and the password is never included in the response. This illustrative password must not be reused.

externalAuthentication.description: Create the Moodle record for a user authenticated by LDAP, without supplying or generating a Moodle-managed password. The ldap authentication plugin must be supported by the site; this request does not create an account in the external directory.

generatedPassword.summary: Create an account and email a generated password
generatedPassword.description: Create a manual-authentication account with initial profile and custom field values. Generate an initial password and email it to the user, who must change it on first login. Email delivery is enabled by default.

bulkProvisioningWithoutEmail.summary: Create an account without sending a credential email
bulkProvisioningWithoutEmail.description: Create an account as part of bulk provisioning, generating an initial password without emailing or returning it. Arrange access separately through password reset or credential provisioning. The creation receipt reports credentialEmailStatus as notRequested.

201.description:
Account and supplied fields created. For generated passwords, `credentialEmailStatus` is:

- `sent`: accepted by the mail transport, not guaranteed inbox delivery.
- `failed`: delivery failed and was logged; the account still exists.
- `notRequested`: email was suppressed.

**Do not repeat POST to retry email delivery.** Passwords are never returned.

Location.description: URL of the created user resource, with its numeric id.

delete.description:
Delete a Moodle account using the normal lifecycle: enrolment/role cleanup, session invalidation, events and auth-plugin notification. **This is not complete personal-data erasure.**

### Permissions

Token scope: `core_user:user:delete`. All callers need system-level `moodle/user:delete`.

Guest accounts, site administrators and your own account are protected (`403`). Missing or already-deleted users return `404`.

### Concurrency and result

Optional `If-Match` uses the ETag from GET `/user/users/{userId}`. A mismatch returns `412` without deletion; omitting it permits unconditional deletion.

Success returns `204` with no body. Repeating the request may return `404`; the account remains deleted.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: Optional ETag of the core user representation. A mismatch returns 412; omitting the header permits unconditional deletion.

204.description: The user account was deleted. No response body.

updateNameAndTimeZone.summary: Update a user's name and time zone
updateNameAndTimeZone.description: Change only the supplied core fields. Other values remain unchanged. The caller must have permission to edit this user, and authentication-plugin field locks still apply.

updateEmail.description: Set a new email address. This administrative field requires moodle/user:update, even when changing the caller's own account. Site email uniqueness rules apply.

suspendAccount.description: Suspend the account and invalidate its active sessions. Requires moodle/user:update. Other core fields remain unchanged.

password.description: Explicit new password satisfying site policy. Never returned.

requirePasswordChange.description: Desired password-change requirement at next login. Omission preserves the current setting.

sendPasswordEmail.description: Email the generated temporary password. Set false to suppress delivery; the password is never returned.

status.description: The credential replacement succeeded. Email delivery is reported independently.

credentialEmailStatus.description: `sent`: accepted by the mail transport, not guaranteed inbox delivery. `failed`: delivery failed and was logged. `notRequested`: email was suppressed.

username.description: Nonblank account username. Do not send an email address in this field unless it is the actual username.

email.description: Email address used to identify an account. Ambiguous matches receive the same generic acceptance response.

username.description: Nonblank, lowercase username satisfying the site's username policy and local-host uniqueness rules.

firstName.description: Must not consist only of whitespace.

lastName.description: Must not consist only of whitespace.

email.description: Must be unique where required by site policy.

auth.description: A supported authentication plugin installed on the site. External authentication provisions the Moodle record only.

password.description: Explicit initial password satisfying site policy. Only permitted for a mechanism using a Moodle-managed password. Mutually exclusive with generatePassword: true.

generatePassword.description: When true, omit password. Generate an initial password and force a password change at first login. Email the password unless sendPasswordEmail is false. Only permitted for a mechanism using a Moodle-managed password. When a password is required, omitting both password and this option is an error.

sendPasswordEmail.description: Controls email delivery when `generatePassword` is true; otherwise this property must be omitted. Defaults to true for generated passwords. Set false for bulk provisioning without credential emails. The generated password is never returned; arrange access separately.

timeZone.description: Valid Moodle time zone. Defaults to the site's default when omitted.

language.description: Installed language code. Defaults to the site's default when omitted.

profile.description: Optional initial profile fields, validated and saved atomically with the account.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, or empty.

customFields.description: Initial custom profile fields. Apply configured defaults for omitted fields and validate required fields, uniqueness and field-type rules before committing account creation.

fields.description: Values keyed by custom profile field shortname, matching the custom-fields resource.

credentialEmailStatus.description:
Present only when `generatePassword` is true.

- `sent`: accepted by the mail transport.
- `failed`: email failed and was logged; the account exists.
- `notRequested`: `sendPasswordEmail` was false.

**Do not retry account creation to resend credentials.**

Problem.description: RFC 9457 problem details with Moodle extensions. Generic HTTP failures may omit `code`. Application-specific codes are stable, non-localised lowercase identifiers; they must not reveal information hidden by an endpoint's public error contract.

code.description: Documented application-specific identifier, independent of the HTTP status and translated message.

errorcode.description: Legacy numeric compatibility member. Its existing meaning is unchanged; use `code` for new application-specific identifiers.

args: The value 'string' was not of type string.

field.description: Request-field path using camelCase API names and dotted nesting, for example `profile.country` or `customFields.fields.studentcode`. Custom field shortnames retain their configured spelling.

code.description: Stable, non-localised validation identifier, for example `invalidemail`, `required`, `unknownfield`, `readonlyfield`, `passwordpolicy` or `incompatibleoptions`.

message.description: Human-readable explanation, which may be translated. Do not echo secrets.

ValidationProblem.description: Well-formed input failed validation. Collect independent errors where practical, without guaranteeing an exhaustive list. Never echo passwords or recovery tokens.

code.description: `usernameexists`: username conflicts with an existing account. `emailexists`: email conflicts where the site requires unique email addresses. `customfieldnotunique`: a supplied custom field violates its configured uniqueness rule.

PasswordRequestThrottled.description: Request-level rate limit exceeded, independently of whether the submitted account exists.

Retry-After.description: Seconds before another request should be attempted.

Forbidden.description: The caller lacks the required token scope or Moodle capability, or the operation targets a protected account, an authentication-plugin-locked field or another non-editable field.

core--router--response--invalid_paramete.description: The request cannot be parsed or structurally interpreted, for example invalid JSON or an uninterpretable parameter encoding. Well-formed input that fails field or parameter validation uses `422`.

ValidationFailure.description: Well-formed input failed field validation: missing required, unknown or read-only fields, invalid values, policy failures or incompatible options. Permission or locked-field failures use `403`; uniqueness conflicts use `409`. Public recovery errors describe input only, never account existence, eligibility or delivery outcomes. Passwords and recovery tokens must not appear in errors.

invalidEmail.description: A field-level code remains stable even when the human-readable message is translated.

UniquenessConflict.description: A username, email (where site policy requires unique addresses) or custom field violates a uniqueness rule. No creation or update is committed.

usernameExists.description: Creation was rejected without creating an account.

value.title: Conflict
value.detail: The username is already in use.

core--router--parameters--query_course.name: course
core--router--parameters--query_course.description:
The course identifier.

This can be the id of the course, the idnumber of the course, or the shortname of the course.

If specifying a course idnumber, the value should be in the format `idnumber:[idnumber]`.

If specifying a course shortname, the value should be in the format `name:[shortname]`.

core--router--parameters--query_coursemo.name: currentmodule
core--router--parameters--query_coursemo.description:
The course module identifier.

This can be the id of the course module or the idnumber of the course module.

If specifying a course module idnumber, the value should be in the format `idnumber:[idnumber]`.

core--router--parameters--query_coursemo.name: coursemodule
core--router--parameters--query_coursemo.description:
The course module identifier.

This can be the id of the course module or the idnumber of the course module.

If specifying a course module idnumber, the value should be in the format `idnumber:[idnumber]`.

core--router--parameters--path_user.name: user
core--router--parameters--path_user.description:
The user identifier.

This can be the magic string 'current', or the user's id, idnumber, or username.

If specifying an id, the value should be in the format `[id]` (for example `42`).

If specifying an idnumber, the value should be in the format `idnumber:[idnumber]`.

If specifying a username, the value should be in the format `username:[username]`.

scopes.core_user:user:delete: Allows the site-wide deletion of user accounts and related data.
scopes.core_user:user:read: Allows site-wide read-only access to any user account and related data, including user profile information and user preferences.
scopes.core_user:user:read:self: Allows read-only access to the current user's own account and related data, including user profile and user preferences.
scopes.core_user:user:update: Allows site-wide updates to user accounts and related data, including user profile and user preferences.
scopes.core_user:user:update:self: Allows update to the current user's own account and related data, including user profile and user preferences.
